Second-team All-Big East (2025) * [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Freshman team (2023) }} '''Alex Karaban''' (born November 11, 2002) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]] of the [[Big East Conference]]. ==Early life and high school career== Karaban was born to Alexi and Olga Karaban, immigrants from Belarus and Ukraine respectively.https://www.ctinsider.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/article/alex-karaban-connecticut-ncaa-tournament-17861149.phphttps://www.ctinsider.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/article/alex-karaban-ncaa-nba-huskies-18396467.php He has two siblings, younger sister Ana and younger brother Andrew.https://www.ctinsider.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/article/alex-karaban-ncaa-tournament-march-madness-boston-19371392.php He grew up in [[Southborough, Massachusetts]], and initially attended [[Algonquin Regional High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.telegram.com/story/sports/college/2023/02/18/former-algonquin-star-alex-karaban-is-shining-as-a-freshman-at-uconn/69915253007/|title='He is wise beyond his years for a freshman': Former Algonquin star Alex Karaban is playing key role at UConn|work=[[Telegram & Gazette]]|date=February 18, 2023|access-date=April 3, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2023/03/31/sports/alex-karabans-living-mens-final-four-dream-with-uconn-that-first-came-him-southborough/|title=Final Four 2023: Inside UConn standout Alex Karaban's journey from Massachusetts to the Final Four|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|date=March 31, 2023|access-date=April 3, 2023}} He transferred to the [[New Hampton School]] in [[New Hampton, New Hampshire]] after his freshman year.{{cite web|url=https://www.telegram.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/01/14/hometeam-change-of-scenery-suits-northboros-alex-karaban/1892391007/|title=Change of scenery suits Northboro's Alex Karaban|work=[[Telegram & Gazette]]|date=January 14, 2020|access-date=April 3, 2023}} Karaban was named the New Hampshire Gatorade Player of the Year as a junior after averaging 25.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 2.9 assists, and 1.9 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2763232/2021/08/11/uconn-gives-alex-karaban-unmatched-opportunity/|title=Forward Alex Karaban sees ‘unmatched’ opportunity as he commits to UConn|first=Charlotte|last=Carroll|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=August 11, 2021|access-date=April 3, 2023}} After two years at New Hampton, he transferred a second time to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]] for one semester before leaving early for UConn. Karaban was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] over offers from [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]], and [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31944350/uconn-huskies-get-commitment-forward-alex-karaban-no-45-2022-class|title=UConn Huskies get commitment from forward Alex Karaban, No. 45 in 2022 class|first1=Jeff|last1=Borzello|first2=Adam|last2=Finkelstein|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=August 2, 2021|access-date=April 3, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.theuconnblog.com/2021/8/2/22569409/four-star-forward-alex-karaban-commits-to-uconn-huskies-mens-basketball-recruiting-class-of-2022|title=Four-star forward Alex Karaban commits to UConn men’s basketball|first=Dan|last=Madigan|website=TheUConnBlog.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=August 2, 2021|access-date=April 3, 2023}} ==College career== Karaban accelerated his graduation at IMG Academy and enrolled at UConn in January 2022.{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/2022/01/07/uconn-recruit-alex-karaban-enrolls-early-joins-mens-basketball-program/|title=UConn recruit Alex Karaban enrolls early, joins men's basketball program|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=January 7, 2022|access-date=April 3, 2023}} He practiced with the team for the rest of the 2021–2022 season and redshirted the year.{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/alex-karaban-uconn-unsung-hero-ncaa-championship-game/xxjs6sjuyykrxg8stnea9eej|title=Redshirt freshman Alex Karaban has shot into position as UConn's 'unsung hero' on march to NCAA Championship game|first=Mike|last=DeCourcy|website=[[Sporting News]]|date=April 3, 2023|access-date=April 3, 2023}} Karaban was a unanimous selection to the [[Big East Conference]]'s All-Freshman team at the end of his redshirt freshman season.{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/2023/03/24/uconn-freshman-alex-karaban-backs-up-his-claim-that-hes-more-athletic-than-he-looks-in-win-over-arkansas|title=UConn freshman Alex Karaban swears he's more athletic than he looks, and showed it in Thursday's Sweet 16|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=March 24, 2023|access-date=April 3, 2023}} He started the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|2023 national championship game]] and scored five points with five rebounds and three blocked shots as the Huskies won 76–59.{{cite web|url=https://www.wcvb.com/article/massachusetts-native-alex-karaban-uconn-basketball-ncaa-championship-game/43500380|title=Massachusetts native starts for UConn in NCAA basketball title game|first=David|last=Bienick|website=[[WCVB-TV|WCVB.com]]|date=April 3, 2023|access-date=April 4, 2023}} Karaban entered his sophomore year on the watchlist for the [[Karl Malone Award]].{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/2023/10/26/uconn-mens-basketballs-alex-karaban-named-to-karl-malone-award-watch-list/|title=UConn men's basketball's Alex Karaban named to Karl Malone Award watch list|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=October 26, 2023|access-date=November 13, 2023}} He scored a career-high 22 points in the Huskies' season-opener against [[2023–24 Northern Arizona Lumberjacks men's basketball team|Northern Arizona]] as UConn won 95–52.{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/banner-uconn-northern-arizona-basketball-de0fb197df381d5c10c0c0ac0e24e6d1|title=No. 6 UConn unveils its 5th championship banner, routs Northern Arizona 95-52 in season opener|first=Pat|last=Eaton-Robb|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 6, 2023|access-date=November 13, 2023}} Karaban averaged 13.3 points and 5.1 rebounds per game as UConn repeated as national champions.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/uconn-forward-alex-karaban-declares-231440753.html|title=UConn forward Alex Karaban declares for NBA draft while retaining college eligibility|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=April 18, 2024|access-date=May 31, 2024}} He initially declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] but ultimately decided to return for his redshirt junior season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/40240815/alex-karaban-withdraw-nba-draft-return-uconn|title=Alex Karaban to withdraw from NBA draft, return to UConn|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=May 29, 2024|access-date=May 31, 2024}} Karaban was one of the people that UConn coach [[Dan Hurley]] consulted when he was offered a head coaching job by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in June 2024.{{Cite news |last=Anthony |first=Mike |date=2024-10-24 |title=UConn coach Dan Hurley wants Alex Karaban 'breathing fire' in pursuit of history, third championship |url=https://www.ctinsider.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/article/alex-karaban-dan-hurley-big-east-uconn-huskies-19856851.php |access-date=2024-10-26 |work=CTInsider.com}} During UConn's senior day on February 28, 2026, Karaban became the first men's player to have been inducted into the [[Huskies of Honor]], an awards program honoring especially impactful players, teams, coaches, and administrators in both men's and women's basketball, while still active at UConn.{{efn|Three other men's players ([[Kemba Walker]], [[Shabazz Napier]], and [[Tristen Newton]]), all of whom were named [[NCAA Division I basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|Final Four Most Outstanding Player]] as seniors on Huskies national championship teams, were inducted upon the Huskies' return from their respective tournament wins. Each of the three championship games was the last UConn game for the honored player.}} By that time, he had become the Huskies' winningest men's player.{{cite news |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/alex-karaban-23-points-lead-192100498.html |title=Alex Karaban’s 23 points lead UConn men to 71-67 win over Seton Hall in final home game |first=Joe |last=Arruda |work=Hartford Courant |publisher=Yahoo Sports |date=February 28, 2026 |access-date=February 28, 2026}} On March 29, 2026, Karaban passed the ball to [[Braylon Mullins]] for Mullins' "miracle" three-point shot that carried UConn over [[2025–26 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] quarterfinal, 73–72.{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=2026-03-29 |title=UConn stuns Duke on Braylon Mullins' miracle last-second triple|url=https://www.espn.com/video/clip/_/id/48342989 |access-date=2026-03-29 |work=espn.com}} ==Career
